prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1203; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: A low-speed collision in a parking lot was reported, and the claimant, who is not represented, reports a shoulder injury. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type.

Entry 2: Took the claimant's account of the collision. The driver is named on the policy, and coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: The police report and witness statements confirm the collision happened as described, and the other driver's account matches. Police and witnesses also confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.

Entry 4: Scene photos were reviewed and show the vehicles in the positions described by the parties. Witnesses and photos are consistent with the reported sequence of events.

Entry 5: Vehicle history and prior claim records show no known earlier damage. Nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 6: The damage photos show dents on a different side of the vehicle and at a different height than the impact the claimant described. The damage pattern does not match the account given.

Entry 7: Medical records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that earlier condition adds to the current complaints.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant gave the same account in every conversation so far. Referred the damage-pattern question to a supervisor for review.

Entry 9: Holding the file open pending a repair estimate review and a supervisor decision on the damage-pattern question before any settlement evaluation.
